content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm attempting to connect a [product_name] module to a TM221 controller to retrieve data. When using Modscan on the [product_name], I can establish a connection via port 510. Is it possible to switch this to port 502? The TM221 controller only accepts connections through port 502. Please refer to the attached Ethernet settings.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. I'm not sure I fully understand your inquiry. Typically with Modbus, port 502 is designated for the server side. Your screenshot shows the [product_name] functioning as a client, with the server-side connecting to port 502 according to the settings provided.

Hi [user_name], My issue is that I cannot directly link the [product_name] to the TM221 controller. The module appears to use port 510, even though the Ethernet configuration specifies port 502. Please see the attached image demonstrating my Modscan connection. Is there a way to change from port 510 to 502?
Are you only using the [product_name] connection to the TM221 controller? If possible, could you upload your [document] diagram as a ZIP file for review?
Hi [user_name], Please find the attached file for your reference.
The [product_name] reserves ports 502 to 509 for up to eight static Modbus server connections. This allocation affects how client connections are handled on Modbus.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face challenges connecting a [product_name] module to a TM221 controller due to Modbus TCP port assignments. The main problem is the [product_name] operating as a Modbus client and using port 510 instead of the standard port 502 required by the TM221. Another user clarifies that the [product_name] reserves ports 502 to 509 for static server connections, which might explain why port 510 is used for client operations. This technical detail causes confusion and complicates integration with third-party PLCs following standard Modbus port conventions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] to connect as a Modbus TCP client to a TM221 controller using the standard port 502 for straightforward integration. They hope to adjust the outgoing port setting to align with third-party PLC requirements.
